findings.source_passage: "Then God keep thee, old man—see'st thou that"—pointing to the hammock—"I bury but one of five stout men
findings.why_it_matters: The draft reassigns the Delight captain's speech — collapsing it into the earlier 'Hast killed him?' exchange and stripping the 'Then God keep thee, old man' opening, which is the signature benediction/curse directed at Ahab and carries heavy interpretive weight as a foreboding judgment.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Then God keep thee, old man' as the captain's direct address before the burial count, preserving that exact phrase.

findings.source_passage: "Oh! God"—advancing towards the hammock with uplifted hands—"may the resurrection and the life——"
findings.why_it_matters: The interrupted burial prayer ('may the resurrection and the life——') is a critical interpretive crux — Ahab's 'Brace forward!' cuts off the sacred words mid-sentence, enacting his blasphemous refusal of Christian consolation. Its absence erases the dramatic and theological point of the scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the captain's advance toward the hammock and the truncated prayer before Ahab's 'Brace forward! Up helm!' interruption.

findings.source_passage: not so quick, indeed, but that some of the flying bubbles might have sprinkled her hull with their ghostly baptism
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'But the suddenly started Pequod'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'ghostly baptism' phrase is a distinctive Melvillean ironic flourish — an anti-baptism answering the blood-baptism of the harpoon — and its loss flattens the symbolic texture of the scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain 'the flying bubbles might have sprinkled her hull with their ghostly baptism' within the corpse-splash sentence.

findings.source_passage: you now saw through this wreck, as plainly as you see through the peeled, half-unhinged, and bleaching skeleton of a horse
findings.why_it_matters: The horse-skeleton simile is a prosodically distinctive Melvillean sentence with the accumulated adjectives ('peeled, half-unhinged, and bleaching') marking the narrator's voice; its excision reduces the wreck description to bare fact.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the horse-skeleton simile as a trailing clause in the description of the shattered whale-boat ribs.

summary: The draft commits two high-severity losses — the 'God keep thee, old man' benediction and the truncated burial prayer that Ahab's command interrupts — plus two medium-severity voice flattenings, collectively gutting the scene's theological and dramatic signature.
